Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to brown velvety spots on leaves and fruit. Leaves may curl and drop prematurely. Fruit shows raised scabby lesions reducing marketability.

pesticide.application: Spray thoroughly on all leaf surfaces

Apple___Apple_scab.organic_remedy: Neem oil spray (5ml/litre) or sulfur-based fungicide
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Plant resistant varieties; maintain proper spacing between trees

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Purple spots on leaves enlarging to brown with purple borders. Fruit shows brown rotting starting at core, eventually turning black and shriveling (mummification).
precautions: Remove mummified fruits from tree and ground
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Remove cankers; maintain tree vigor through proper nutrition

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright orange-yellow spots on upper leaf surface with tube-like structures underneath. Infected fruit shows orange lesions. Causes early defoliation.

pesticide.frequency: Every 7-10 days from pink bud stage

precautions: Remove nearby juniper/cedar trees if possible
Apply fungicides during wet spring weather
Monitor for orange galls on cedar trees nearby
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Plant rust-resistant apple varieties; create distance from cedar trees

Apple___healthy.symptoms: No disease symptoms. Plant shows normal green foliage and healthy fruit development.
precautions: Monitor regularly for early disease signs
Apple___healthy.prevention: Regular monitoring and good agricultural practices

Blueberry___healthy.symptoms: No disease detected. Plant exhibits healthy green leaves and normal berry development.
Blueberry___healthy.organic_remedy: Regular organic mulching with acidic material
precautions: Mulch with pine bark to retain moisture
Blueberry___healthy.prevention: Proper soil preparation and pH management

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery coating on young leaves, shoots, and fruit. Infected leaves curl upward and may turn yellow. Severely affected shoots become stunted.

pesticide.application: Spray during early morning or evening

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.organic_remedy: Baking soda solution (5g/litre) or potassium bicarbonate
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Plant in sunny locations with good air flow; choose resistant varieties

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.symptoms: No disease detected. Plant shows healthy green foliage and normal fruit set.
precautions: Water at base to keep foliage dry

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Rectangular gray-tan lesions parallel to leaf veins. Lesions have distinct borders and may coalesce causing large dead areas. Severely affected plants show premature death of lower leaves.

pesticide.frequency: At tasseling and again 2 weeks later
pesticide.application: Aerial or ground application; cover all leaf surfaces

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.prevention: Use resistant hybrids; practice crop rotation with non-host crops

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Small, circular to elongate cinnamon-brown pustules on both leaf surfaces. Pustules rupture releasing powdery rust spores. Severe infection causes yellowing and death of leaves.

pesticide.frequency: At first sign of disease; repeat in 7-14 days

precautions: Plant early to avoid heavy infection periods
Monitor fields regularly especially after cool/humid nights
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention: Use rust-resistant varieties; early planting dates

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long (5-15 cm), cigar-shaped gray-green to tan lesions on leaves. Lesions have wavy edges and grayish appearance due to spore production. Can cause significant yield loss.

pesticide.application: Apply before disease reaches upper canopy

precautions: Crop rotation with soybean or small grains
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Resistant hybrids are most effective; combine with crop rotation

Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: No disease detected. Plant shows healthy green leaves and normal growth.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.prevention: Good agronomic practices and regular monitoring

Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Tan-brown circular lesions with dark borders on leaves. Infected berries turn brown, shrivel, and become hard black mummies. Can destroy entire crop if untreated.

pesticide.frequency: Every 7-10 days from bud break through veraison
pesticide.application: Thorough coverage of all vine parts

precautions: Remove infected canes during dormant pruning
Keep disease-free during critical infection periods (bloom to fruit set)
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Resistant varieties; canopy management for air flow

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: Tiger-stripe pattern of yellowing on leaves. Berries develop dark spots and may crack. Internal wood shows dark streaking. Chronic form causes gradual vine decline.

pesticide.chemical: No fully effective chemical control exists
pesticide.dosage: Wound sealants (Topsin-M paste) on pruning cuts
pesticide.application: Paint on all pruning wounds immediately

precautions: Remove and burn severely infected vines
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).prevention: Use certified disease-free planting material; proper pruning hygiene

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Irregular dark brown spots on upper leaf surface with grayish fungal growth beneath. Severely infected leaves turn yellow and drop. Reduces photosynthesis and fruit quality.

pesticide.application: Spray both upper and lower leaf surfaces

precautions: Apply fungicides preventively in humid conditions

Grape___healthy.symptoms: No disease detected. Vine exhibits healthy green foliage and normal bunch development.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Asymmetric yellowing (blotchy mottle) on leaves. Fruits remain small, green, bitter, and misshapen. Shoots die back. Trees decline progressively and die within years.

pesticide.dosage: 0.5 ml per litre for foliar; soil drench as label directed
pesticide.application: Focus on new flush growth where psyllids feed

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).organic_remedy: Reflective mulches to repel psyllids; kaolin clay sprays
precautions: REMOVE AND DESTROY infected trees immediately
Control Asian citrus psyllid vector aggressively
Do not transport plant material from infected areas
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).prevention: Use certified disease-free nursery stock; aggressive psyllid control

Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked lesions on leaves becoming angular, dark, and eventually falling out (shot-hole). Fruit shows pitted, scabby spots reducing quality. Severe cases cause defoliation.

pesticide.application: Begin at shuck split; cover all surfaces

precautions: Reduce tree stress through proper nutrition
Apply protective sprays before rain events
Peach___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Plant resistant varieties; minimize plant wounding

Peach___healthy.symptoms: No disease detected. Tree shows healthy green foliage and normal fruit development.
Peach___healthy.organic_remedy: Dormant oil spray in late winter as preventive
precautions: Annual pruning for open center structure
Peach___healthy.prevention: Good sanitation; remove fallen fruit and leaves

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, water-soaked circular spots on leaves with yellow halos turning dark brown. Fruit shows raised, warty, dark spots. Severe infections cause defoliation and fruit drop.

pesticide.dosage: 2 g copper + 1.5 g mancozeb per litre
pesticide.frequency: Every 5-7 days in warm humid weather
pesticide.application: Begin at transplanting; thorough coverage essential

precautions: Rotate with non-solanaceous crops (3 year rotation)
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use resistant varieties; crop rotation; avoid overhead irrigation

Pepper,_bell___healthy.symptoms: No disease detected. Plant shows healthy dark green leaves and normal fruit set.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.organic_remedy: Seaweed extract foliar spray for plant immunity
Pepper,_bell___healthy.prevention: Good cultural practices and balanced fertilization

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown to black concentric ring lesions (target-board pattern) on older leaves first. Yellow halo around lesions. Tubers may show dark, sunken lesions at harvest.

pesticide.application: Begin spraying when plants are 15-20 cm tall

Potato___Early_blight.organic_remedy: Copper sulfate or Bacillus subtilis-based products
precautions: Rotate crops — avoid potatoes/tomatoes in same field consecutively
Hill soil around plants to protect tubers
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Use certified seed potatoes; avoid stressing plants

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked pale green lesions on leaves turning dark brown/black quickly. White mold visible on leaf undersides in humid conditions. This was the cause of the Irish Famine — extremely destructive.

pesticide.chemical: Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (Ridomil Gold MZ) or Cymoxanil
pesticide.application: PREVENTIVE application is crucial — apply before infection

precautions: NEVER use infected tubers as seed
Remove and destroy all infected material immediately
Store harvested tubers in cool, dry, well-ventilated area
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Resistant varieties; destroy volunteer potato plants; monitor weather forecasts

Potato___healthy.symptoms: No disease detected. Plant shows healthy green canopy and normal tuber development.
Potato___healthy.prevention: Crop rotation and good seed selection

Raspberry___healthy.symptoms: No disease detected. Canes show healthy green leaves and normal fruit development.
precautions: Remove old fruited canes after harvest

Soybean___healthy.symptoms: No disease detected. Plant shows uniform green color and normal pod development.
Soybean___healthy.prevention: Crop rotation and proper seed treatment

Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery patches on upper leaf surfaces, stems, and petioles. Infected leaves turn yellow then brown and die. Reduces fruit size and quality. Very common in late summer.

pesticide.application: Cover upper and lower leaf surfaces; spray in morning

Squash___Powdery_mildew.organic_remedy: Potassium bicarbonate or milk spray (40% milk:60% water)
precautions: Do not apply sulfur when temperature exceeds 32°C
Squash___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Plant resistant varieties; ensure adequate spacing; avoid wet foliage

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Irregular dark purple spots on upper leaf surface. Spots enlarge and centers turn tan/gray. Severely affected leaves look scorched. Weakens plants and reduces yield.
precautions: Remove and destroy old infected leaves
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.prevention: Use resistant varieties; proper plant spacing; certified transplants

Strawberry___healthy.symptoms: No disease detected. Plant shows healthy trifoliate leaves and normal fruit production.
Strawberry___healthy.prevention: Regular plant renewal and good sanitation

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, water-soaked circular spots on leaves with yellow halos; centers turn dark brown. Fruit shows raised, scabby, dark spots reducing marketability. Causes defoliation in severe cases.
precautions: Use disease-free seed treated with hot water
Avoid working when foliage is wet
Stake and prune for air flow
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Resistant varieties; certified seed; drip irrigation

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown concentric ring spots (bullseye pattern) on older lower leaves first. Yellow tissue surrounds lesions. Stem lesions (collar rot) can girdle seedlings. Reduces fruit quality.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Crop rotation; resistant varieties; good plant spacing

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, greasy-looking gray-green to dark brown lesions on leaves and stems. White mold on leaf undersides in humid weather. Fruit shows large, firm, dark brown lesions. Extremely fast-spreading.

pesticide.chemical: Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (Ridomil Gold) or Cymoxanil + Mancozeb
pesticide.frequency: Every 5-7 days; more frequently in cool/wet weather
pesticide.application: Preventive application is critical before infection

precautions: DESTROY infected plants and fruit immediately
Do not compost infected material — burn or bag it
Monitor weather — infection favors cool (10-24°C), wet conditions
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Resistant varieties; eliminate potato volunteers nearby; regular scouting

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale green to yellow patches on upper leaf surface. Corresponding velvety olive-gray mold growth on leaf undersides. Infected leaves curl upward and die. Most common in greenhouses.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Resistant varieties; humidity management; proper plant spacing

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Numerous small (3-6mm) circular spots with dark brown borders and light gray-white centers. Tiny black dots (pycnidia) visible in spot centers. Causes severe defoliation starting from lower leaves.

pesticide.application: Begin at first sign; ensure complete coverage

precautions: Remove and destroy lower infected leaves
Stake plants to minimize soil splash
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Resistant varieties; crop rotation; mulching; drip irrigation

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine yellow stippling on upper leaf surface. Fine webbing visible on leaf undersides. Leaves turn bronze, then yellow-brown and die. Severe infestations cause complete leaf death in hot dry weather.

pesticide.application: Thorough coverage of leaf undersides essential

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.organic_remedy: Neem oil (5ml/litre) + soap; predatory mite releases (Phytoseiulus)
precautions: Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides that kill natural enemies
Increase humidity (mites thrive in dry conditions)
Rotate miticide groups to prevent resistance
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.prevention: Encourage natural predators; adequate irrigation; early detection

Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Circular to irregular brown spots with concentric rings on leaves. Lesions may have yellow halo. Fruit shows small, sunken, dark spots. Can cause significant defoliation and fruit loss.
precautions: Remove infected leaves and plant debris
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention: Good sanitation; resistant varieties where available

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Young leaves curl upward and inward, turn yellow at margins. Severe stunting of plants. Flowers drop, fruit set is poor. Transmitted by whiteflies — plants infected early may produce no fruit.

pesticide.chemical: Imidacloprid (Confidor) or Thiamethoxam for whitefly vector
pesticide.dosage: 0.5 ml per litre (foliar) or soil drench
pesticide.application: Target whitefly adults and nymphs on leaf undersides

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.organic_remedy: Yellow sticky traps; reflective mulch; neem oil for whiteflies
precautions: NO CURE — infected plants must be REMOVED AND DESTROYED
Control whitefly populations aggressively and early
Do not transplant near infected fields
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: TYLCV-resistant varieties are the most effective strategy; aggressive whitefly control

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mosaic pattern of light and dark green mottling on leaves. Leaves may show distortion, blistering, or fern-leaf symptoms. Fruit shows yellowing and internal browning. Plants may be stunted.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.organic_remedy: Skim milk spray (10%) as preventive to block virus transmission
precautions: Disinfect tools with 10% bleach solution or trisodium phosphate
Wash hands with soap before handling plants
Do NOT use tobacco products near tomatoes (can carry virus)
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Resistant varieties (Tm-2 gene); certified virus-free seed; strict sanitation

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: No disease detected. Plant shows deep green healthy leaves and normal fruit development.
Tomato___healthy.organic_remedy: Compost tea spray; calcium foliar spray for blossom end rot prevention
precautions: Monitor regularly for early disease/pest signs
Consistent watering to prevent blossom end rot
Tomato___healthy.prevention: Good cultural practices; balanced fertilization; regular scouting
